chunks: From al-Nadr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Zayd al-Shahham who said, 'I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:'
Beware of the violent strikes of Allah by night and by day. So I asked, 'What are the violent strikes of Allah?' He said, 'His punishment for sins.'

key_terms.سَطَوَاتِ اللَّهِ: Violent strikes or sudden punitive actions of Allah

ai.seo_question: What does 'satawat Allah' mean in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) warns believers to be cautious of Allah's sudden punitive strikes (satawat) during both night and day, emphasizing the unpredictability of divine retribution. He defines these strikes as Allah's taking hold of the sinner as a consequence of their disobedience, a concept deeply rooted in Shia hadith literature where 'satawa' denotes a swift, unexpected seizure of the soul or state. This teaching encourages constant vigilance (muraqabah) in daily life, reminding the faithful that divine justice is not limited to specific times but can occur at any moment.
